entries.claim: Feed ranking predicts like, scroll-past without engaging, reply, post click, profile click, permalink dwell time, view time and reply-to-reply engagement (about 50 signals, no weights published). Repost, quote and follow prediction are not listed.
entries.hypothesis: Posts that invite a considered reply and hold the reader longer get more reach than posts that only earn a like.

entries.claim: Posts that drive conversations are more likely to be recommended, and replies account for almost half of the views on Threads.
entries.hypothesis: Ending a post on a concrete opinion others can answer produces more replies and more views than a closed statement.

entries.claim: Meta reports that text on a video, photo or carousel raises views, and that funny content gets more views.
entries.hypothesis: A post with one image and a text line gets more views than the same text alone.

entries.claim: Posting more often goes with more impressions per post; Meta suggests 2 to 5 posts a week.
entries.hypothesis: Holding a steady posting rhythm lifts views per post compared with bursts and gaps.

entries.claim: A post carries one topic tag, and the first valid tag is the one applied.
entries.hypothesis: Placing the single most relevant topic tag first gets a post to the right audience.

entries.claim: Posts with a topic tag generally get more views (Meta internal data, not independently measured).
entries.hypothesis: Tagged posts get more views than untagged posts of the same kind from this account.

entries.claim: Every word of a post is searchable in all languages, and search results are ranked, not chronological.
entries.hypothesis: Naming the searched term plainly in the post text brings more views from search than a paraphrase.

entries.claim: Ranking was rebalanced toward accounts a user follows, so follower growth matters for reach.
entries.hypothesis: Content that earns a follow, measured as followers gained per 1,000 views, compounds later reach.

entries.claim: Link posts have been ranked properly since mid-2025, but few readers click links.
entries.hypothesis: A link post reaches as many people as a text post but earns fewer clicks, so the value must sit in the post text.

entries.claim: Communities are out of beta and among the fastest-growing Threads features.
entries.hypothesis: Posting in a community that matches the account topic reaches readers the feed does not.

entries.claim: Authors who reply to comments see about 42% more engagement (within-account comparison, n=128k posts, correlational).
entries.hypothesis: Replying to early comments on our own posts lifts engagement on those posts.

entries.claim: Best times are Thursday 9am and Wednesday 12pm or 9am, and weekends are weakest (Western data, n about 2.5M posts; it contradicts Meta's weekend claim and is untested for Vietnam).
entries.hypothesis: Posting at the Buffer peak slots in the audience's local time beats other slots for this account.

entries.claim: Consistent weekly posting goes with 4.5 times the engagement per post (n over 100k users, cross-platform, correlational).
entries.hypothesis: Posting on a fixed weekly rhythm lifts engagement per post compared with irregular posting.

entries.claim: Format studies conflict: video 5.55% against text 2.79% (Buffer 2026, 45M posts, cross-platform), images first and text last (Buffer 2025, no n), and on Threads text 1.89% per impression against images 0.99% and video 0.53% (Ordinal).
entries.hypothesis: For this account, a text-only post and an image post differ in engagement per view; measure before choosing a format.

entries.claim: Hedged wording goes with about 25% more engagement, controlling for length, links and verification (n=16,695 tweets, Arabic).
entries.hypothesis: Opinions phrased with a hedge ("I think", "usually") earn more engagement than flat assertions.

entries.claim: Text-only tweets did best at 120 to 140 characters (1M tweets, old X data).
entries.hypothesis: Posts of about 140 characters earn more engagement than posts of 400 or more.

entries.claim: The first line decides whether a reader scrolls past, which is a ranker signal; hooks, curiosity gaps and contrarian takes have no rigorous data.
entries.hypothesis: A first line that states the specific point earns fewer scroll-pasts than a vague teaser.

entries.claim: Hook formulas (curiosity gap, contrarian take) are practitioner opinion with no measured effect.
entries.hypothesis: A contrarian opening line earns more replies than a neutral one on the same topic.

entries.claim: Replying early under accounts 2 to 10 times our size works better than replying under mega-accounts (practitioner; a skeptical view exists).
entries.hypothesis: A substantive early reply under an account 2 to 10 times our size brings profile visits and followers.

entries.claim: Posting on a story before interest peaks earns more reach than posting after it; hour cut-offs are unverified.
entries.hypothesis: A post on a trend within hours of its first appearance earns more views than one a day later.

entries.claim: A named recurring series, a branded tag, a consistent voice and replying to every comment went with 195k views in 17 days (one Vietnamese account's own case study).
entries.hypothesis: A recurring named series earns more returning readers than standalone posts.

entries.claim: Bragging is a native Threads genre in Vietnam (an estimated 6 to 7 of 10 posts) and readers tire of it.
entries.hypothesis: Self-deprecating or specific-result posts earn more engagement than plain bragging from the same account.

entries.claim: No Threads-specific peak hours exist for Vietnam; Facebook's 13h to 16h and 19h to 21h are a proxy only.
entries.hypothesis: Posts at 19h to 21h Vietnam time earn more views than posts at other hours.

entries.claim: Explicit requests for votes, shares, comments or tags are demoted as engagement bait. The policy page names Facebook, and Meta acknowledged engagement bait rising on Threads. A closing call-to-action question can collide with this.
entries.hypothesis: A post that earns replies through its content alone, with no request to comment, reaches as far as one that asks for comments.

entries.claim: Threads aims to reduce rage-bait posts, content built to anger readers at people.
entries.hypothesis: Disagreement aimed at an idea instead of a person keeps reach that provocation aimed at people loses.

entries.claim: Unoriginal or aggregated reposts lose recommendations; a repost needs commentary of our own.
entries.hypothesis: A repost with our own added take earns more views than a bare repost.

entries.claim: Political content is not proactively recommended on Threads.
entries.hypothesis: Posts on political topics reach fewer non-followers than posts on the account's own topics.
